problem_statement: Developers integrating LangChain with enterprise infrastructure cannot reliably authenticate or secure transport across provider integrations. ChatAnthropic lacks support for supplying a custom HTTP client or TLS configuration, which blocks certificate-based authentication and SSL customization required in locked-down enterprise networks. Separately, proxy layers sitting in front of MCP servers do not correctly forward or propagate authentication headers to downstream servers, producing 403 authentication failures even when the original request was properly authenticated. Provider integrations also handle httpx client construction inconsistently between Azure OpenAI and base OpenAI paths, leading to duplicated or misconfigured clients that carry auth/transport settings and waste connections. Finally, the SSRF protection layer's environment-variable-based allowlist matching can be bypassed, meaning the authorization boundary that is supposed to prevent requests to unauthorized internal/external hosts cannot be trusted as-is. Together these gaps mean there is no consistent, secure way to configure and enforce authentication and transport security across LangChain's provider and proxy surfaces.
target_user: Developers and platform engineers integrating LangChain-based applications with enterprise authentication infrastructure (mTLS, certificate-based auth, custom proxies, and internal network allowlists) across model providers (Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) and MCP server deployments

user_stories.persona: a developer deploying ChatAnthropic behind an enterprise proxy requiring client certificates
user_stories.action: supply a custom HTTP client with TLS/certificate configuration to ChatAnthropic
user_stories.value: I can authenticate to Anthropic's API through my organization's certificate-based security requirements without forking the library

user_stories.persona: a platform engineer running an MCP proxy in front of downstream MCP servers
user_stories.action: have authentication headers correctly forwarded and propagated from the proxy to downstream MCP servers
user_stories.value: authenticated requests do not fail with spurious 403 errors caused by dropped or malformed headers

user_stories.persona: a developer maintaining integrations across Azure OpenAI and base OpenAI providers
user_stories.action: use a consistent, shared httpx client configuration path for auth and transport settings across both providers
user_stories.value: I avoid redundant connections and unpredictable auth/transport behavior caused by divergent client handling

user_stories.action: have SSRF/allowlist validation logic that cannot be bypassed via environment variable manipulation
user_stories.value: the authorization boundary protecting internal and restricted hosts remains enforced regardless of environment configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: a developer instantiates ChatAnthropic with a custom HTTP client configured for mTLS
acceptance_criteria.when: a request is made to the Anthropic API
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is sent using the supplied client's TLS/certificate configuration instead of a default client

acceptance_criteria.given: an MCP proxy receives an authenticated request with a valid auth header
acceptance_criteria.when: the proxy forwards the request to a downstream MCP server
acceptance_criteria.then: the auth header is propagated unmodified and the downstream server does not return a 403 due to missing/malformed auth

acceptance_criteria.given: a developer configures a custom httpx client for either Azure OpenAI or base OpenAI
acceptance_criteria.when: requests are made through either provider integration
acceptance_criteria.then: both providers use the same client-construction code path and apply the supplied auth/transport settings identically

acceptance_criteria.given: an environment variable is set that matches an internal/restricted host pattern
acceptance_criteria.when: the SSRF/allowlist validation logic evaluates a request to that host
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is blocked and no environment-variable-based bypass allows it through

acceptance_criteria.given: no custom HTTP client is supplied to ChatAnthropic
acceptance_criteria.then: existing default behavior is preserved with no regression in default (non-mTLS) requests

acceptance_criteria.given: a security test suite targeting the SSRF allowlist bypass
acceptance_criteria.then: all previously passing bypass reproduction cases now fail to bypass the allowlist

out_of_scope: Adding new authentication protocols beyond certificate-based/mTLS and existing header-based auth
Building a UI or dashboard for managing certificates or credentials
Auditing or hardening authentication for provider integrations not named in this finding (e.g., other LLM providers not mentioned)
General MCP proxy performance or feature work unrelated to auth header propagation
Rewriting the full SSRF protection architecture beyond fixing the environment-variable bypass

risks.description: The evidence base is thin: three of the four pain points have a frequency of only 1, meaning most of this PRD rests on a single reported issue each, with limited corroboration of scope or user impact.
Introducing custom HTTP client support in ChatAnthropic could introduce inconsistent behavior or regressions in default (non-custom-client) request paths if not carefully scoped.
Fixing SSRF allowlist bypass logic touches a core security boundary; an incomplete fix could give a false sense of security while leaving related bypass vectors open.

Unifying httpx client handling across Azure OpenAI and base OpenAI may require coordinated changes across multiple integration modules, risking scope creep beyond the immediate auth/transport concern.
